newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso erases gains on pacto fears,ends lower.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso erases gains on pacto fears,ends lower.

text.p: The Mexican peso relinquished ground that it had clawed back to close weaker against the dollar for the fifth session in a row on Thursday.
Traders said the downturn came on speculation triggered by the forthcoming renewal of the government's economic pact with business and labor, traders said.
"The peso was under pressure after midsession due to speculation over the pacto...someone stepped in to buy a hefty (dollar) position, and it snowballed from there," said a trader.

The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour equivalent ended down 2.2 and 1.25 centavos, respectively, at 7.8675/7.8720 and 7.8500/7.8575 per dollar. The same-day peso closed ealier 2.65 centavos firmer at 7.8050/7.8135 per dollar.
The "pacto", now known as the Alliance for Economic Recovery, is the economic agreement signed annually by government, labor and business leaders in Mexico since 1987.
Minister of Labor Javier Bonilla said on Thursday that no date had been fixed for signing a renewal of the pacto. Traders speculated, however, that the "pacto" might be signed this coming weekend.
"Wage and price hikes to be inked into the new pacto are causing concern," said a trader.

The peso had recovered earlier from the speculative battering it took on Wednesday on a favorable outlook for inflation figures and on traders buying pesos to invest in the Mexican money market over the weekend.
Traders said that inflation figures for the first half of October, due later on Thursday, could determine how the peso fares on Friday.
A Reuters survey of traders showed they expected an average rise of 0.74 percent in consumer prices, compared to a 1.6 percent rise for all of September.
